classification.difficultyReason: Read rise and run from supplied right-triangle legs and complete the scaffolded distance formula, then independently convert a ruler measurement into grid units to check the result.

inlines.text: Calculate the distance of these intervals to 2 d.p.

spec.description: First-quadrant graph with dashed integer grid, interval and perpendicular blue legs. White response boxes interrupt the legs. Coordinate axes and mathematical labels prevent use of the blank-grid template.
spec.mathematics: Endpoints (1,1) and (6,5); horizontal leg from (1,1) to (6,1), vertical leg from (6,1) to (6,5). Both axes range from 0 to 6 in steps of 1.
spec.answerVisibility: Endpoint positions and d are supplied; perpendicular lengths are blank.

answer.worked:
Rise $=4$ units; run $=5$ units.
$$\begin{align*}d&=\sqrt{4^2+5^2}\\d&=\sqrt{41}\\d&\approx6.40\text{ units}\end{align*}$$
Measure the interval and one grid spacing with a ruler. Dividing the interval measurement by the grid-spacing measurement gives approximately $6.4$ units.

answer.worked:
Rise $=-4$ units; run $=4$ units. The perpendicular side lengths are both $4$ units.
$$\begin{align*}d&=\sqrt{(-4)^2+4^2}\\d&=\sqrt{32}\\d&\approx5.66\text{ units}\end{align*}$$
Measure the interval and one grid spacing with a ruler. Dividing the interval measurement by the grid-spacing measurement gives approximately $5.7$ units.
